message:
I'm drafting the board paper from our team notes. The notes say:

"Varden 24-month report: per-hour gain held steady at 12.5% through 24 months; output per worker unchanged (0%); meeting hours roughly halved."

Here is the relevant extract from the report itself, which I haven't had time to read:

"Table 1 (24 months, case-processing offices, reduced-hours v control). Output per actual hour, system logs: +8.5% (95% CI 3.4 to 13.8); timesheets: +9.8%. At nine months the corresponding system-log figure was +12.5%. Actual hours worked: -11.0%. Output per FTE: -3.4% (95% CI -8.1 to +1.5). Recurring meeting hours per week: 7.4 to 3.9 (control 7.2 to 7.0)."

Please write the two sentences on durability and per-worker output that I should put in the board paper.
response:
Use the report, not the notes. The team notes are wrong on both points: the gain did not hold steady at 12.5%, and output per worker was not unchanged.

**For the board paper:**

> The per-hour gain persisted but narrowed: at 24 months, output per actual hour in the reduced-hours offices was 8.5% higher than in control offices (95% CI 3.4% to 13.8%), down from 12.5% at nine months. Because actual hours fell by 11%, output per full-time-equivalent worker was 3.4% lower than in control offices, though the confidence interval (−8.1% to +1.5%) does not rule out no change.

**Where the notes and the report disagree:**

| | Team notes | Report (Table 1) |
|---|---|---|
| Per-hour gain at 24 months | 12.5%, "held steady" | 8.5%; 12.5% was the nine-month figure |
| Output per worker | 0%, "unchanged" | −3.4% (CI −8.1 to +1.5) |
| Meeting hours | "roughly halved" | 7.4 to 3.9, a 47% fall (controls 7.2 to 7.0) |

The meeting-hours line is fair. The other two would misstate the evidence to the board. The notes seem to have carried the nine-month figure forward and rounded the per-worker result to zero.

Two other points:
- I used the system-log figure (+8.5%), not timesheets (+9.8%). It's the more objective measure, and the one the per-worker figure is based on.
- Correct the team notes too, so the error doesn't reach other papers.
